**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the user area after failed boot0 checks**

When the supplied SHA-256 is invalid, the preceding `range(1, ...)` has already selected boot0 through `device()`, but this branch returns without calling `device(0, ...)`. The same state leak occurs on several allocation/alignment error exits in `hash_range()`, `export_range()`, and `erase()`. After any such expected validation failure, the MMC remains on boot0, so a recovery command that uses the current MMC hardware partition (for example a raw `mmc read`/`mmc write`) can unexpectedly access boot0. Route all post-selection exits through cleanup that restores the user area.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
